summary:
Items 1 and 8 of the list "What still needs your word" hold 3 real choices and 6 closed things. I wrote 3 open decisions (D-PRE-01 to D-PRE-03), one section fragment for each, closed.md, and notes.md. All files are below /Users/diegohaz/.claude/jobs/f65a6229/tmp/round7/decisions/validator-logs. I changed no file below the worktree, made no Git or GitHub write, and sent no request to production.

Check that ran: the stable copy of revision r7 plus the 3 decisions and the 3 fragments passes `node apps/lab/audit/build.mjs --check` (61 decisions, 0 warnings). `check.mjs` (the Chrome check) did not run.

Item 1, the validator. The only server check of image bytes today is this (counted from code, apps/web/src/api/workflow-owned.ts:1038-1044):

    if (bytes.byteLength !== image.bytes || (await sha256(bytes)) !== image.digest) {
      throw new SecurityError("image_mismatch", 422, "The image digest or size differs.");
    }

After D-OPS-04, one of the 5 accounts with push access (measured today) can replace the Submit job. It can then store bytes that are not a PNG, 2 MiB at most for each capture, or a PNG whose header declares another size. It cannot change the type (always image/png, with nosniff and a sandbox policy: images.ts:48-57), cannot submit for another repository, commit, or fork (oidc.ts:150-156, 210-212, 300), cannot change the baseline of main (baseline-promotion.ts:114, 380), and cannot approve (api/index.ts:190-205).

The worst realistic result with no new check: in one pull request, a reviewer sees an error text in place of a screenshot, and the check stays open until a new run. The review page of today already decodes each opened image, compares its size, and keeps Approve off (screenshot-viewer.tsx:49-71). The worst case needs a second failure, a replaced Submit job that is merged to main. No byte check closes that case, because the same job can send a valid PNG with wrong pixels.

Cost of "the service checks the bytes", measured in Node, not in a Worker. All options add 0 D1 writes.
- PNG header (33 bytes): below 0.01 ms, about 15 lines. It refuses non-PNG bytes and a false header size. It accepts damaged image data.
- Structure parse (validateImage in the web Worker): 1.3 ms at 23 KB, 14 ms at 295 KB, 61 ms at 2 MiB; about 10 lines plus 529 lines of validators in the Worker; about 84 MB if 5 parses run in one isolate (a calculation). It refused all 4 bad test files.
- Full decode in the comparison Worker: takes back the answer to D-CODE-02; the 1,935 lines of apps/compare stay.

Item 8, the two logs.
- The pass log is the Cloudflare Worker log (apps/web/src/operations/index.ts:103-109). Only a person with access to the Cloudflare account reads it (assumption: the account was not read). It is not public.
- The CLI message goes to the Submit job log of the consumer. ariakit/ariakit is public (measured today). The capture job of run 37671649487 already prints the file and the title of each of its 212 tests in the same public log (measured today).

decisions.question: After your answer to D-OPS-04, a pull request can replace the Submit job. Then no program opens the image files before the service stores them. Must the service open them itself?
decisions.options: 1. size-and-digest-only: no check of the content, keep the size and the digest, and say the limit in the contract. 2. png-header: read the PNG signature and the header size, 33 bytes, about 15 lines. 3. png-structure: parse the PNG structure with validateImage in the web Worker (14 ms at 295 KB in Node). 4. full-decode-worker: keep the comparison Worker and call POST /validate for each upload (takes back the answer to D-CODE-02).
decisions.recommended: 1. size-and-digest-only. Reasons: the headers of the image address stop a script for each kind of bytes; the review page does not show a file that the browser cannot decode at the stored size; no byte check stops a valid PNG with wrong pixels. Wrong if the service must refuse non-image bytes as a rule or before a second customer (then option 2), or if contract line 24 must stay true as written (then option 3).

decisions.question: When a background pass fails, may its log line say the kind of error and the HTTP status that GitHub answered?
decisions.options: 1. step-only: the fields of row 7 as accepted, the failed step and no cause. 2. fixed-cause: add errorName, code, and upstreamStatus, each from a list in the source code, never a message or a stack. 3. message-text: also add the first 200 characters of the error message.
decisions.recommended: 2. fixed-cause. Reasons: the values are listed in the source code, so they are not a raw exception, and the second auditor read contract line 81 in the same way; the log is private; 0 D1 writes. Wrong if line 81 means "no value from an error object" (then option 1), or if the failures to diagnose are D1 failures, for which the fixed fields say only "Error" (then option 3).

decisions.question: When Submit fails because of one screenshot, may the message of the CLI name that screenshot in the CI log?
decisions.options: 1. no-names: the code and the reference of the service only, as accepted with D-CODE-01. 2. keys-in-message: print the item key, the variant key, and the two numbers, never the display title. 3. keys-in-debug-run: print the keys only when the job runs with RUNNER_DEBUG=1.
decisions.recommended: 2. keys-in-message. Reasons: the same public log already holds the file and the title of each test (measured today), and a key can hold only letters, digits, and . _ / - (packages/protocol/src/validate.ts:131-139), so it cannot hold a line break or a log command. Wrong if the CLI output must hold no consumer data as a rule (then option 1), or if a later customer makes keys from private data (then option 3).

closed: C1. The contract sentence about the validator. Closed by "3. Ok". The contract pull request changes docs/current-contract.md lines 24, 32, 48 (row D03), and 188 as D-CODE-02 says. Only the words of the sentence about the limit wait for D-PRE-01; closed.md has the sentence for each option. Record: 45-code-ci-docs.html, anchor code-comparison-worker, note "Revision r4", and the rationale of D-CODE-02.

C2. The removal of the comparison Worker (the three steps of D-CODE-02). Closed by "I authorize the implementation". It changes only if D-PRE-01 gets option 4: then the removal stops after step 2. The read of the Worker request count in Cloudflare is in item 3 of the list, which another part handles.

C3. The two image checks of the review page go into the new page. Closed by "I authorize the implementation". Keep element.decode() and the size comparison (apps/web/src/components/screenshot-viewer.tsx:49-71) and the Approve gate (review-workspace.tsx:302-307). The lab stage tests only that an image loaded (apps/lab/src/explorations/kits/ariakit/stage/canvas.tsx:73). Give non-image bytes their own text: today it says "Check your connection and retry" (screenshot-viewer.tsx:158). The record does not state this today; the fragment of D-PRE-01 states it.

C4. Row 7 of D-OPS-01 without the cause (message kind, attempt, queue wait, failed step, time and counts of each step). Closed by the settled answer to D-OPS-01 and "I authorize the implementation". No D1 write, ordinary service deployment. D-PRE-02 decides only the cause fields.

C5. The code and the reference of the service in a CLI message (row PKG-02 of D-CODE-01). Closed by "I authorize the implementation", "the package publication", and "the change in ariakit/ariakit". Read the error body for each refused status (packages/cli/src/http.ts:175), let beginSubmission pass a CliError (bundle-submit.ts:69-71), and put it in the same CLI release as the change of D-OPS-04.

C6. Contract line 81, if D-PRE-02 adds fields. Closed by "3. Ok". Option 2 adds three field names to the list of line 81; option 3 also changes the words "raw exception". The same edit names the optional fields runId and taskId that the code already writes (apps/web/src/operations/failure.ts:22-23). Item 9 of the list does not name line 81 today.

List cleanup: when the three decisions are in the page, item 1 becomes a link to D-PRE-01 and item 8 becomes links to D-PRE-02 and D-PRE-03. Row 7 of the table of D-OPS-01 ("needs your word") and the bullet "Failure cause" above D-CODE-01 ("need your yes: write it in the notes") get the same links.
wrongInRecord: Row 7 of the table of D-OPS-01 (35-state-checks.html, lines 309 to 315 in r7) and item 8 of the list: they say that contract line 81 forbids a raw exception in the pass log. Line 81 is about the operation-failed line of a failed request ("that log"). The pass writes another line, operations_pass (apps/web/src/operations/index.ts:103-109). The rule for the pass log is the code comment at operations/failure.ts:13 and the row D13 at contract line 57. The sense is the same; the cited line is not exact.

Contract line 81 against the code, not named in section 35: line 81 lists "fixed operation, code, correlation ID, and elapsed-time fields", and the code also writes runId and taskId when it has them (apps/web/src/operations/failure.ts:22-23).

The rationale of D-OPS-04, the rationale of D-CODE-02, and the note "Revision r4" say that in a run with a replaced Submit job "nothing decodes the images". Not complete: the review page of today decodes each image that a reviewer opens, compares its size with the stored size, and keeps Approve off until then (screenshot-viewer.tsx:49-71, review-workspace.tsx:302-307). The service also checks the declared type and the declared size (apps/web/src/api/local-comparison.ts:535 and 548).

Item 1 of the list names one remedy, "the last option of D-CODE-02". Two smaller checks exist: the PNG header (33 bytes) and the structure parse in the web Worker. The option text of D-CODE-02 names the parse only in its last sentence.

The bullet "Failure cause" above D-CODE-01 asks for a yes to capture names in a public CI log. It does not say that the capture job of the same run already prints the file and the title of each test in the same public log (measured today: 212 lines in job 112966055554 of run 37671649487).

apps/lab/audit/reports/gap-trust-boundary/report.md:97 ("Bytes that are not a PNG: No, the CLI decodes each capture") is true only while the Submit job runs the CLI. The record already says this in the note "Revision r4"; the report is history and needs no edit.

Checked and correct: 5 accounts with push access; 1 approval in the branch rule (also code owner review and approval of the last push); "about 2,000 lines" for the comparison Worker (1,935 counted); lines 1038 to 1044 as the only server check of bytes; "about 85 MB" for 5 parses (my calculation: 84 MB); 14 ms for the parse at 2.06 megapixels.
doubts: No browser test: I did not open a non-PNG file or a PNG with a header of 30,000 by 30,000 pixels in a browser. The error text that the reviewer sees comes from the code (screenshot-viewer.tsx:155-161). The memory that a tab uses for the large header is not known.
No Worker measurement: each time of the byte checks is from Node v24.18.0 on the audit computer. CPU time and memory in a Worker are not measured.
The line counts of the options (about 15, 10, 20, and 30 lines) are estimates. Nobody built the header check, the parse call, the log fields, or the CLI messages.

Who can read each log: I did not read the Cloudflare account, so the access to the Worker log and its retention are assumptions. I read the job logs of ariakit/ariakit with the account of the maintainer, so "each GitHub user can read them" comes from the GitHub documentation, not from a test.
RUNNER_DEBUG=1 (option 3 of D-PRE-03) comes from the GitHub documentation and was not tested.

The settled answers to D-WORK-04 and D-WORK-06 let one decision cover images that nobody opened, and a whole-screenshot decision tests only the shown variant (review-workspace.tsx:385-394). So the review page check protects only an image that a reviewer opens. D-PRE-01 says this as a limit of option 1. I did not reopen those two decisions. If the maintainer wants the review page to be the last validator, that is a new question for the workspace section.

D-PRE-03 can be too small for a panel: the evidence points one way and each option is cheap. I made it a decision because the record asked for a yes and the authorization of the implementation does not name what a public log may hold. The coordinator can fold it into D-CODE-01 if the maintainer wants fewer panels.

Option 2 of D-PRE-01 (PNG header) accepts a PNG with damaged image data (measured). I kept it because it is the only check with no CPU cost and no memory cost that refuses bytes that are not an image.
check.mjs did not run. The draft passes build.mjs --check, but the look of the three fragments in Chrome at 400 px is not checked. The fragment of D-PRE-01 has 3 wide tables that scroll in their box.

The places of the fragments come from the stable copy of revision r7. Sections 35 and 45 are not in the list of sections that r8 changes, but if r8 moves the placeholders of D-OPS-01, D-CODE-01, or D-CODE-02, the places move with them.
The D1 error text in the fragment of D-PRE-02 shows the form of a D1 error. It is not a recorded line, and the fragment says so.

Not checked again: the deploy step of 7 s and the 2 failures in 78 deploy runs, the 27 ms for parse and decode, the 4 answers of 503 for 5 calls, and the count of 3,582 captures of a run. The decisions cite them from the record or from the comparison lane.
